claim: Most studies of auditory segregation have used relatively simple signals, in contrast to the complex acoustic environments encountered in everyday life.
source_text: In contrast to the complex acoustic environments we encounter everyday, most studies of auditory segregation have used relatively simple signals.
evidence_reasoning: This is a general statement about the state of the field, drawing on established knowledge and implicitly referencing prior literature on auditory segregation studies.

claim: Human listeners are remarkably sensitive to the emergence of coherent patterns ('figures') from overlapping 'background' signals in the stochastic figure-ground stimulus.
source_text: In a series of experiments, we demonstrate that human listeners are remarkably sensitive to the emergence of such figures
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from the psychophysical experiments reported in the manuscript.

claim: Human listeners can tolerate a variety of spectral and temporal perturbations when detecting figures in the stochastic figure-ground stimulus.
source_text: we demonstrate that human listeners are remarkably sensitive to the emergence of such figures and can tolerate a variety of spectral and temporal perturbations.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from experiments 3-6 which tested various perturbations.

claim: The observed behavior in figure detection is consistent with the existence of automatic auditory segregation mechanisms that are highly sensitive to correlations across frequency and time.
source_text: This robust behavior is consistent with the existence of automatic auditory segregation mechanisms that are highly sensitive to correlations across frequency and time.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing robust performance across various conditions.

claim: The observed behavior in figure detection cannot be explained purely on the basis of adaptation-based models used to explain the segregation of deterministic narrowband signals.
source_text: The observed behavior cannot be explained purely on the basis of adaptation-based models used to explain the segregation of deterministic narrowband signals.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the experimental results and comparison with predictions from adaptation-based models.

claim: The experimental results are consistent with the predictions of a model of auditory perceptual organization based on temporal coherence.
source_text: We show that the present results are consistent with the predictions of a model of auditory perceptual organization based on temporal coherence.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the modeling results presented in Figure 3 and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, which show agreement between model predictions and behavioral data.

claim: Temporal coherence plays a role as an organizational principle underlying auditory segregation.
source_text: Our data thus support a role for temporal coherence as an organizational principle underlying auditory segregation.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental and modeling data presented in the study.

claim: The separation of mixtures of sounds into perceptually distinct sound sources is a highly complex task.
source_text: Although we do it effortlessly, the separation of such mixtures of sounds into perceptually distinct sound sources is a highly complex task.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement based on established scientific understanding of auditory processing.

claim: The neural bases of auditory object formation and segregation still remain to be fully explained.
source_text: In spite of being a topic of intense investigation for several decades, the neural bases of auditory object formation and segregation still remain to be fully explained
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: A sequence of two pure tones alternating in time can 'stream' or segregate into two sources under certain conditions.
source_text: The most commonly used signal for probing auditory perceptual organization is a sequence of two pure tones alternating in time that, under certain conditions, can 'stream' or segregate into two sources
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations to van Noorden (1975) and Bregman (1990).

claim: Fishman and colleagues observed spatially segregated responses to two tones in the auditory cortex of macaques for large frequency differences and fast presentation rates.
source_text: For large frequency differences and fast presentation rates, which promote two distinct perceptual streams, they observed spatially segregated responses to the two tones.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Fishman et al. (2001; 2004).

claim: The pattern of segregated cortical activation has been proposed to underlie the streaming percept.
source_text: This pattern of segregated cortical activation, proposed to underlie the streaming percept, has since been widely replicated
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to replication studies.

claim: Segregated cortical activation in streaming has been attributed to basic physiological principles of frequency selectivity, forward masking and neural adaptation.
source_text: This pattern of segregated cortical activation, proposed to underlie the streaming percept, has since been widely replicated (e.g., Bee and Klump, 2004; 2005; Micheyl et al., 2007a; Bidet-Caulet and Bertrand, 2009) and attributed to basic physiological principles of frequency selectivity, forward masking and neural adaptation
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Fishman and Steinschneider (2010a) and other studies.

claim: Frequency selectivity, forward masking and neural adaptation contribute to stream segregation by promoting the activation of distinct neuronal populations in the primary auditory cortex that are well separated along the tonotopic axis.
source_text: These properties are considered to contribute to stream segregation by promoting the activation of distinct neuronal populations in the primary auditory cortex (A1) that are well separated along the tonotopic axis
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations and represents established theoretical understanding.

claim: Human imaging studies have shown correspondence between the streaming percept and underlying neural activity in A1.
source_text: Human imaging studies that directly correlated the perceptual representation of streaming sequences with brain responses also support the correspondence between the streaming percept and the underlying neural activity in A1
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to multiple imaging studies.

claim: Similar segregation effects have been demonstrated in the auditory nerve, suggesting that processes contributing to segregation might occur earlier in the ascending auditory pathway.
source_text: However, similar effects have also been demonstrated in the auditory nerve, suggesting that processes contributing to segregation might occur earlier in the ascending auditory pathway rather than be mediated exclusively by the auditory cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is based on cited studies and involves inference about the location of segregation processes.

claim: The streaming paradigm uses relatively simple, temporally regular narrowband signals which do not capture the rich spectrotemporal complexity of natural acoustic scenes.
source_text: A major drawback of the streaming paradigm is that it uses relatively simple, temporally regular narrowband signals which do not capture the rich spectrotemporal complexity of natural acoustic scenes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a critical assessment based on understanding of both the streaming paradigm and natural acoustic environments.

claim: Informational masking refers to a type of non-energetic or central masking associated with an increase in detection thresholds due to stimulus uncertainty and target-masker similarity.
source_text: IM refers to a type of non-energetic or central masking that is associated with an increase in detection thresholds due to stimulus uncertainty and target-masker similarity that is distinct from peripheral energetic masking
evidence_reasoning: This is a definition supported by citations to the informational masking literature.

claim: Target detection in informational masking experiments is critically dependent on the width of the spectral protection region and the density of the maskers.
source_text: Results demonstrate that target detection is critically dependent on the width of the spectral protection region, and the 'density' of the maskers
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to multiple studies on informational masking.

claim: Informational masking has been hypothesized to rely on the same adaptation-based mechanisms as proposed in the context of simple streaming signals.
source_text: has been hypothesized to rely on the same adaptation-based mechanisms as proposed in the context of simple streaming signals
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis from the literature, supported by citation to Micheyl et al. (2007b).

claim: Sounds in everyday life are often broadband with multiple frequency components that are temporally correlated and overlap with other signals in the environment.
source_text: In contrast, the sounds we are required to segregate in everyday life are distinct from the narrowband targets used in streaming and IM paradigms; they are often broadband with multiple frequency components that are temporally correlated and overlap with other signals in the environment
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the nature of natural sounds based on general scientific understanding.

claim: When two tones in a streaming signal are presented synchronously, listeners perceive the sequence as one stream irrespective of the frequency separation between the two tones.
source_text: Recently, Elhilali et al. (2009a) demonstrated that when the two tones in a streaming signal are presented synchronously, listeners perceive the sequence as one stream irrespective of the frequency separation between the two tones
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from a cited study by Elhilali et al. (2009a).

claim: The finding that synchronous tones are perceived as one stream is inconsistent with predictions based on adaptation-based models.
source_text: a result that is inconsistent with predictions based on adaptation-based models
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about model predictions based on the cited experimental result.

claim: Temporal coherence between different elements in the scene is essential for segregation such that temporally incoherent patterns tend to result in a segregated percept while temporal coherence promotes integration.
source_text: Instead, the authors argued that in addition to separation in feature space, temporal coherence between different elements in the scene is essential for segregation such that temporally incoherent patterns tend to result in a segregated percept while temporal coherence promotes integration
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical argument from cited literature.

claim: The stochastic figure-ground stimulus consists of coherent ('figure') and randomly varying ('background') components that overlap in spectrotemporal space and vary only in their statistics of fluctuation.
source_text: we developed a new stimulus (Stochastic figure-ground; SFG) consisting of coherent ('figure') and randomly varying ('background') components that overlap in spectrotemporal space and vary only in their statistics of fluctuation
evidence_reasoning: This describes the stimulus design created by the authors for their experiments.

claim: Listeners achieved mean hit rates of 93 ± 2% for the most salient coherence/duration combination in experiment 1.
source_text: Hit rates (not shown) mirror d′ with listeners achieving mean hit rates of 93 ± 2% for the most salient coherence/duration combination.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of experimental data from experiment 1.

claim: The patterns in the stochastic figure-ground stimulus were very brief (longest figure duration was 7 chords or 350 ms), yet very high levels of performance were observed.
source_text: It is notable that the patterns were very brief (longest figure duration was 7 chords or 350 ms), yet very high levels of performance were observed (and without extensive practice).
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation based on the experimental data and stimulus parameters.

claim: High performance on brief patterns without extensive practice is consistent with the idea that the task taps low-level, finely tuned segregation mechanisms.
source_text: This is consistent with the idea that this task based on the SFG stimulus taps low-level, finely tuned segregation mechanisms.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the observation of high performance on brief patterns.

claim: A global power increase per se associated with the emergence of the figure can be discounted as a potential cue for figure detection.
source_text: Since 'figure-absent' and 'figure-present' signals were controlled for overall number of components (see 'Materials and methods'), a global power increase per se associated with the emergence of the figure, can be discounted as a potential cue.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the experimental design which controlled for the number of components.

claim: Listeners achieved hit rates of 92 ± 3% for the highest coherence/duration combination in experiment 3 with 25 ms chords.
source_text: Listeners achieved hit rates of 92 ± 3% for the highest coherence/duration combination used.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of experimental data from experiment 3.

claim: Performance in figure detection largely depends on the number of repeating chords irrespective of the time scale.
source_text: An ANOVA with coherence and duration as within-subject factors and experimental condition (50 ms vs 25 ms chords) as a between-subject factor revealed no significant effect of condition (F1,15 = 2; p=0.174), suggesting that performance largely depends on the number of repeating chords irrespective of the time scale.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from statistical analysis of experimental data comparing experiments 1 and 3.

claim: Maximum hit-rates of 0.97 and 0.83 were obtained for figures with coherence equal to 8 and duration equal to 7 for ramp levels of 2 and 5 respectively in experiment 4.
source_text: Performance in these experiments was robust (maximum hit-rates of 0.97 and 0.83 were obtained for figures with coherence equal to 8 and duration equal to 7 for the two ramp levels of 2 and 5 respectively)
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of experimental data from experiment 4.

claim: Performance was significantly worse for the ramp = 5 vs ramp = 2 condition in experiment 4.
source_text: Performance was significantly worse for the ramp = 5 vs ramp = 2 condition (F1,18 = 21, p<0.001)
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from statistical analysis of experimental data.

claim: Listeners exhibited above-chance performance even for the steeper slope (ramp = 5) in experiment 4.
source_text: but, remarkably, listeners exhibited above-chance performance even for the steeper slope.
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The segregation mechanisms are more susceptible to spectral than temporal perturbations.
source_text: This suggests that the segregation mechanisms in question are more susceptible to spectral than temporal perturbations (as in experiments 3, and 6 below) but can still integrate over dynamically changing, rather than fixed, figure components.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from comparing performance across different experimental manipulations.

claim: Listeners reached hit rates of 89 ± 5% for the most salient condition in experiment 5 with isolated figures.
source_text: Similar to previous experiments, the results (Figure 4C) show a marked effect of coherence and duration, and performance improved with increasing salience of the figures with listeners reaching hit rates of 89 ± 5% for the most salient condition.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of experimental data from experiment 5.

claim: The 'background-only' chords which preceded the figure did not affect performance in figure detection.
source_text: To evaluate behavior with respect to experiment 1, an ANOVA with coherence and duration as within-subject factors and experimental condition (with background vs no background) as a between-subject factor was used which yielded no significant effect of condition: F1,16 = 0.033; p=0.859, suggesting that the 'background-only' chords which preceded the figure did not affect performance.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from statistical analysis comparing experiments 1 and 5.

claim: Maximum hit rate of 0.93 was obtained for the most salient condition in experiment 6a with chords interrupted by noise.
source_text: The results (Figure 4D) show good behavioral performance (maximum hit rate of 0.93 was obtained for the most salient condition)
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of experimental data from experiment 6a.

claim: Interleaving noise bursts between successive chords does not affect figure detection performance.
source_text: An ANOVA with coherence and duration as within-subject factors and experimental condition (50 ms repeating chords vs 50 ms chords alternating with white noise) as a between-subject factor revealed no significant effect of condition (F1,17 = 0.004; p=0.953). Interleaving the noise bursts between successive chords does not therefore affect performance.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from statistical analysis comparing experiments 1 and 6a.

claim: Listeners showed robust performance for all durations of noise up to 300 ms in experiment 6b.
source_text: Results (Figure 4E) indicate robust performance for all durations of noise up to 300 ms
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from experimental data in experiment 6b.

claim: Listeners showed supra-threshold performance (d′ = 1.00 ± 0.30) for a noise duration of 500 ms in experiment 6b.
source_text: and surprisingly, supra-threshold performance (d′ = 1.00 ± 0.30; significantly different from 0: p=0.01; t = 3.29) for a noise duration of 500 ms.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: Listeners can integrate coherent patterns over 3 s long temporal windows (in the case of 500 ms noise bursts).
source_text: This remarkable ability of listeners to integrate coherent patterns over 3 s long (in the case of 500 ms noise bursts) suggests that the underlying higher-order mechanisms are very robust over such long time windows.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about integration time based on the experimental data from experiment 6b.

claim: Temporal windows of integration as long as 500 ms have rarely been reported in the context of auditory object formation in complex scenes.
source_text: Temporal windows of integration, as long as 500 ms, have rarely been reported in the context of auditory object formation in complex scenes such as those examined here.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding based on knowledge of the literature.

claim: The results suggest the existence of a central mechanism that integrates repeating pure tone components as belonging to a distinct object over multiple time scales.
source_text: The results suggest the existence of a central mechanism that is not affected by interfering broadband noise that integrates repeating pure tone components as belonging to a distinct object over multiple time scales.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results, particularly experiment 6b.

claim: The long temporal windows implicate cortical mechanisms at or beyond primary auditory cortex.
source_text: The long temporal windows here implicate cortical mechanisms at or beyond primary auditory cortex (see e.g., Overath et al., 2008 demonstrating a range of 'cortical windows' between 20 ms and 300 ms).
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about neural mechanisms based on the temporal characteristics of the behavior, supported by citation.

claim: Fast detection with minimal training of the stochastic figure-ground stimulus was demonstrated.
source_text: We demonstrate fast detection with minimal training of a novel figure-from-ground stimulus comprising an overlapping figure and ground segment
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary of the experimental findings across all experiments.

claim: In the stochastic figure-ground stimulus, the figure has multiple components that are temporally coherent: they start and stop together.
source_text: where, like natural stimuli, the figure has multiple components that are temporally coherent: they start and stop together.
evidence_reasoning: This describes a key property of the stimulus design.

claim: Figures in the stochastic figure-ground stimulus can be detected as objects that can be distinguished, consistent with a high-level mechanism for object detection.
source_text: We show that such figures can be detected as objects that can be distinguished, consistent with a high-level mechanism for object detection as opposed to the simple detection of frequency or modulation cues (experiment 2).
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the results of experiment 2 (AXB task).

claim: The figure detection mechanism scales in time, in that detection depends on the number of components over time rather than their absolute duration.
source_text: The mechanism scales in time, in that detection depends on the number of components over time rather than their absolute duration (experiment 3)
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the results of experiment 3 comparing 50 ms and 25 ms chords.

claim: The figure detection mechanism can still operate if the object is defined by slowly changing frequency trajectories rather than a fixed set of frequencies.
source_text: and can still operate if the object is defined by slowly changing frequency trajectories rather than a fixed set of frequencies (experiment 4).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from experiment 4 with ramped figures.

claim: The figure detection mechanism is robust to interruption of the figure by interleaved noise.
source_text: It is robust to interruption of the figure by interleaved noise (experiment 5)
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from experiment 6a.

claim: The figure detection mechanism can operate over a remarkably long timescale.
source_text: and can operate over a remarkably long timescale (experiment 6).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from experiment 6b showing performance with 500 ms noise interruptions.

claim: Modeling based on temporal coherence demonstrated a similar profile to the behavioral results.
source_text: Modeling based on temporal coherence demonstrated a similar profile to the behavioral results
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary of the modeling results presented in Figure 3 and supplements.

claim: This study constitutes the first demonstration of the compatibility of the temporal coherence model with segregation in complex acoustic scenes.
source_text: and constitutes the first demonstration of the compatibility of the temporal coherence model with segregation in complex acoustic scenes.
evidence_reasoning: This is a claim about the novelty of the work based on the modeling and experimental results.

claim: The temporal coherence model proposes that segregation is determined by the temporal relationship between different elements in the scene.
source_text: The temporal coherence model proposes that segregation is determined not only based on separation in feature-space but rather by the temporal relationship between different elements in the scene
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the temporal coherence model from cited literature.

claim: According to the temporal coherence model, temporally coherent elements are grouped together, while temporally incoherent channels with independent fluctuation profiles are perceived as belonging to separate sources.
source_text: such that temporally coherent elements are grouped together, while temporally incoherent channels with independent fluctuation profiles are perceived as belonging to separate sources
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the temporal coherence model from cited literature.

claim: The temporal coherence model incorporates a feature analysis stage that performs multidimensional feature analysis by distinct populations of neurons in the auditory cortex.
source_text: Specifically, the model incorporates two stages: firstly, a feature analysis stage that performs multidimensional feature analysis by distinct populations of neurons in the auditory cortex that are tuned to a range of temporal modulation rates and spectral resolution scales.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the temporal coherence model from cited literature.

claim: A pair of synchronous repeating tones produces the same coherent pattern of modeled central activity as a single stream irrespective of the frequency separation between them.
source_text: they showed that a pair of synchronous repeating tones produces the same coherent pattern of modeled central activity as a single stream irrespective of the frequency separation between them
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from cited work by Elhilali et al. (2009a).

claim: Synchronous and alternating cortical responses were equally segregated despite their perceptual differences, indicating that temporal factors are more important in inducing the one and two streams percept.
source_text: This was substantiated by direct neurophysiological recordings from ferret auditory cortex which showed that synchronous and alternating cortical responses were equally segregated despite their perceptual differences, and hence that the temporal factors are more important in inducing the one and two streams percept
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from cited neurophysiological studies.

claim: Temporal coherence is modulated as a function of the coherence and the duration of the figure in a manner similar to the modulation of figure detection performance.
source_text: In the case of the more complex SFG stimuli, the modeling results suggest that temporal coherence is modulated as a function of the coherence and the duration of the figure in a manner similar to the modulation of figure detection performance.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the modeling results presented in the study.

claim: Temporal coherence may serve as a correlate of stimulus salience by which the brain picks out the most important sounds in busy auditory scenes.
source_text: The data suggest temporal coherence as a correlate of stimulus salience by which the brain picks out the most important sounds in busy auditory scenes
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the experimental and modeling results.

claim: Temporal coherence may be achieved by binding across distributed feature channels without significant changes in ensemble activity.
source_text: a process that may not be computed by dedicated structures but could be achieved by binding across distributed feature channels without significant changes in ensemble activity.
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about how temporal coherence might be implemented neurally.

claim: Similar accounts of binding in vision based on coherence of the temporal structure have been put forward previously.
source_text: Similar accounts of binding in vision based on coherence of the temporal structure have been put forward previously
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about related work in vision, supported by citations.

claim: It is not known how temporal coherence may be computed and which brain areas perform these computations.
source_text: It is still not known how temporal coherence may be computed and which brain areas perform these computations.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Temporal coherence may be implemented by neurons that show strong sensitivity to temporal coherence across distant frequency channels, or by neurons that act as multiplexers.
source_text: Temporal coherence may be implemented by neurons that show strong sensitivity to temporal coherence across distant frequency channels, or by neurons that act as multiplexers and are more selective to particular combinations of inputs
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative statement about possible neural implementations, based on cited theoretical work.

claim: Elhilali et al. were unable to demonstrate neurons sensitive to temporal coherence in the primary auditory cortex of passively listening ferrets.
source_text: Elhilali et al. (2009a) sought such cells in the primary auditory cortex of the ferret but were unable to demonstrate any in passively listening animals
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from cited work by Elhilali et al.

claim: Elhilali et al. have preliminary evidence of neurons sensitive to temporal coherence in behaving ferrets.
source_text: but have preliminary evidence in behaving ferrets
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about unpublished or preliminary findings from cited authors.

claim: Previous brain imaging studies have identified activity in A1 that was correlated with the streaming percept.
source_text: Although previous brain imaging studies have identified activity in A1 that was correlated with the streaming percept (e.g., Gutschalk et al., 2005; Snyder et al., 2006; Wilson et al., 2007)
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary of findings from cited imaging studies.

claim: No evidence of modulation of BOLD signal in A1 as a function of figure emergence was found in a passive listening paradigm using the stochastic figure-ground stimulus.
source_text: we found no evidence of modulation of BOLD signal in A1 as a function of figure emergence in a passive listening paradigm (Teki et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from a previous study by the authors.

claim: Activity in the intraparietal sulcus (IPS) was strongly modulated by the salience of the figure in the stochastic figure-ground stimulus.
source_text: However, we found activity in the intraparietal sulcus (IPS) to be strongly modulated by the salience of the figure, similar to the modulation of temporal coherence observed here.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from a previous study by the authors (Teki et al., 2011).

claim: The IPS activation likely reflects bottom-up stimulus-driven processing of figures.
source_text: The IPS activation likely reflect bottom-up stimulus-driven processing of figures
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the IPS activation finding.

claim: Areas outside the conventional auditory system, such as the parietal cortex, may have a role in auditory segregation.
source_text: and is consistent with accumulating literature which suggests that areas outside the conventional auditory system, such as the parietal cortex may have a role in auditory segregation
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about trends in the literature, supported by citations.

claim: Attention influences auditory segregation.
source_text: Although not relevant to the passive fMRI experiment (Teki et al., 2011), attention also influences segregation.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement of established knowledge in the field.

claim: The parietal cortex receives auditory input from the temporoparietal cortex.
source_text: In this regard, the parietal cortex is in an ideal position to integrate both bottom-up auditory input as it receives auditory input from the temporoparietal cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is anatomical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The parietal cortex receives top-down attentional input from the prefrontal cortex.
source_text: as well as top-down attentional input from the prefrontal cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is anatomical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: IPS is associated with both bottom-up and top-down attention.
source_text: IPS is associated with both bottom-up and top-down attention
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about IPS function.

claim: IPS is a key structure implicated in saliency map models of visual search.
source_text: and is a key structure implicated in saliency map models of visual search
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the role of IPS in vision, supported by citations.

claim: In saliency map models, low-level feature maps may combine with top-down cognitive biases to represent a global saliency map.
source_text: where low-level feature maps may combine with top-down cognitive biases to represent a global saliency map
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of saliency map models from cited literature.

claim: IPS has been implicated in mediating object representations, binding of sensory features within and across different modalities, as well as attentional selection.
source_text: IPS (and its monkey homologue) has been implicated in mediating object representations, binding of sensory features within and across different modalities, as well as attentional selection.
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary of established knowledge about IPS function, implicitly supported by the literature.

claim: IPS may represent a neural correlate of the figure percept where the representation will depend on the salience of auditory figures.
source_text: We hypothesize that IPS may represent a neural correlate of the figure percept where the representation will depend on the salience of auditory figures.
evidence_reasoning: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their findings.

claim: In the proposed model, the perceptual representation of figures depends on the computation of temporal coherence across multiple frequencies that are initially represented in the auditory cortex.
source_text: In our model, this perceptual representation depends on the computation of temporal coherence across multiple frequencies that are initially represented in the auditory cortex.
evidence_reasoning: This is a theoretical statement about the proposed model.

claim: The stochastic figure-ground stimulus consists of a sequence of random chords, each 50 ms in duration with 0 ms inter-chord-interval, presented for a total duration of 2000 ms.
source_text: Figure 1 presents examples of the SFG stimulus which consists of a sequence of random chords, each 50 ms in duration with 0 ms inter-chord-interval, presented for a total duration of 2000 ms (40 consecutive chords).
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the stimulus design.

claim: Each chord in the stochastic figure-ground stimulus contains a random number (average: 10 and varying between 5 and 15) of pure tone components.
source_text: Each chord contains a random number (average: 10 and varying between 5 and 15) of pure tone components.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the stimulus design.

claim: The spectral components in the stochastic figure-ground stimulus are randomly selected from a set of 129 frequencies equally spaced on a logarithmic scale between 179 Hz and 7246 Hz.
source_text: The spectral components are randomly selected from a set of 129 frequencies equally spaced on a logarithmic scale between 179 Hz and 7246 Hz such that the separation between successive components is 1/24th of an octave.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the stimulus design.

claim: In half of the stochastic figure-ground stimuli, a random number of tones are repeated across a certain number of consecutive chords which results in the percept of a 'figure' that pops out of the random tonal background.
source_text: In half of these stimuli, a random number of tones are repeated across a certain number of consecutive chords (e.g., in Figure 1, four components marked by arrows are repeated across 6 chords) which results in the percept of a 'figure' that readily pops out of the random tonal background.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the stimulus design and the perceptual effect it produces.

claim: To eliminate correlation between the number of figure and background components, the figure was realized by first generating the random background and then adding additional, repeating components to the relevant chords.
source_text: To eliminate correlation between the number of figure and background components, the figure was realized by first generating the random background and then adding additional, repeating components to the relevant chords.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the stimulus generation procedure to control for confounds.

claim: In the stochastic figure-ground stimulus, 50% of stimuli containing no figure also included additional tonal components which changed from chord to chord and did not form a coherent figure.
source_text: To avoid the problem that the interval containing the figure might, on average, also contain more frequency components, and to prevent listeners from relying on this feature in performing the figure detection task, the remaining 50% of the stimuli (those containing no figure) also included additional tonal components, which were added over a variable number (2–7) of consecutive chords at the same time as when a figure would have appeared. But these additional components changed from chord to chord and did not form a coherent figure.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the stimulus design to control for potential confounds.

claim: The onset of the figure in the stochastic figure-ground stimulus was jittered between 15 and 20 chords (750–1000 ms) post stimulus onset.
source_text: The onset of the figure was jittered between 15 and 20 chords (750–1000 ms) post stimulus onset.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the stimulus design.

claim: All participants tested reported normal hearing and had no history of audiological or neurological disorders.
source_text: All participants tested in this set of experiments reported normal hearing and had no history of audiological or neurological disorders.
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the participant inclusion criteria.

claim: Experimental procedures were approved by the research ethics committee of University College London.
source_text: Experimental procedures were approved by the research ethics committee of University College London (Project ID number: 1490/002), and written informed consent was obtained from each participant.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about ethical approval for the research.

claim: The temporal coherence model takes the spectrogram of the stimulus as its input and simulates spectral analysis performed at the level of the cochlea and temporal integration at the level of the auditory cortex.
source_text: The first stage takes the spectrogram of the stimulus as its input and simulates spectral analysis performed at the level of the cochlea and temporal integration at the level of the auditory cortex
evidence_reasoning: This is a description of the temporal coherence model from cited literature.

claim: Temporal integration in the temporal coherence model is achieved through a bank of bandpass filters that are tuned to different physiologically plausible parameters.
source_text: This temporal integration is achieved through a bank of bandpass filters that are tuned to different physiologically plausible parameters that capture the rich variety of spectrotemporal receptive fields (STRFs) found in A1.
